On a RYDE_POOL trip the POL-RD-01 baseline is the matched-itinerary optimal recorded in trip_record.optimal_distance_km, and that is 19.4 km — the platform's pooled quote for Punggol to the Hougang co-rider pickup and on to Raffles Place, as the trip_record's optimal_route_source states. A claim that measures excess against the solo optimal has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone.

The governing distance is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which POL-RD-01 makes the deciding field precisely because trip_record.actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test. The trace is 20.18 km against a matched-itinerary optimal of 19.4 km — an excess of 0.78 km and 4.02%. Both POL-RD-01 tests must pass. 0.78 km is not greater than the 0.8 km absolute threshold and 4.02% is not greater than the 20% percentage threshold, so no deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The result does not turn on which distance field is read. Even taking the trip_record's own rounded 20.2 km, the excess over the 19.4 km matched itinerary is 0.80 km — not GREATER than the 0.8 km absolute threshold POL-RD-01 requires, since that test is strict — and 4.1%, nowhere near the 20% percentage threshold. On either reading both establishment tests fail and no deviation exists however the rider characterises the trip.

The Hougang leg the rider complains about is a platform-matched co-rider pickup, not a driver detour. POL-RD-12 excludes distance attributable to collecting a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied. The system chat message sent at 18:42:04, before the trip started at 18:47:10, reads 'Co-rider matched. Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min' — the same 19.4 km the trip_record stores as the matched-itinerary optimal. The driver simply drove the route the app displayed to him.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. The trace here is unimpaired: 100% coverage, 217 fixes, no gaps, a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds and a 10-second sampling interval against an expected 10 seconds. On that clean trace the excess is only 0.78 km. The burden is not discharged.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be established under POL-RD-06. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 471, so both the count test (3 or more) and the ratio test (0.05 or more, with at least 40 completed trips) fail. POL-RD-06 is not engaged, and in any event it can never be used to establish that this particular trip deviated.

I do not rely on traffic-closure exoneration, and I say why on the record: EV-ADVIS-00113-01 carries no payload and is a MISSING artifact at weight 0.0, so no advisory covers this corridor and POL-RD-03 cannot be run. That absence costs the driver nothing here, because the deviation fails POL-RD-01 on the threshold arithmetic alone and the driver needs no exculpatory clause to defeat it.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02's optimal-route recomputation never runs and the charged fare stands as billed. POL-GEN-03 makes that outcome NO_ACTION, which on this rider-filed dispute leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd at 0.0: the driver retains the SGD 26.83 legitimately billed for driving the matched pooled itinerary the platform assigned him.
